decisions.reason: The building data digital twin service disappeared from the website by 2024 and, for a medium-sized geospatial IT firm with a broad portfolio, that usually signals limited traction or a shift back to stronger core offerings.

The authentication and identity delegation service gained its own page in 2024, indicating growing relevance and a good strategic fit with enterprise and public-sector demand for secure integration of GeoIT into existing systems.

An open GIS application development framework fits the firm's R&D-oriented, platform-based business model and can support both customer projects and reusable components even if it is marketed less prominently than full services.

The identity and access service was given dedicated positioning in 2024 and directly addresses a recurring customer need to connect GIS applications with existing user management, making it strategically valuable.
The geodata business process consulting workshop extends the established consulting business, has low product risk, and can generate follow-on implementation work, so it is sensible to continue.
